Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Third Quarter Fiscal 2025 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad followed by one. To withdraw your question, press star two. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Third Quarter Fiscal 2025 earnings call. Joining me today are Sarah Chen, CEO; Mike Patel, CFO; Dr. Elena Vasquez, CTO; Jordan Lee, Chief Revenue Officer; Lisa Wong, Chief Product Officer; Tom Harris, Chief Marketing Officer; and Rachel Kim, Chief Customer Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge's performance for the third quarter of fiscal 2025. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our ForgeAI platform and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on eight key areas: ARR growth year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter, cash runway, CAC trends, free cash flow, LTV to CAC ratio, full-year revenue guidance, Rule of 40, and operating margin.

These metrics underscore the strength and predictability of our cloud-native DevOps platform, which powers CI/CD pipelines, GitOps workflows, and AI-driven deployment automation for over 5,000 customers worldwide. We're confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Patel to discuss the financials in more detail.

Mike Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $152 million, representing a 37% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 82%, and operating income was $43 million.

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand our product offerings. Our cash position remains strong at $452 million, providing us with the flexibility to pursue strategic acquisitions and other growth opportunities.

We are updating our full-year guidance to reflect our strong performance in the first three quarters of the year. We now expect revenue to be in the range of $605 million to $615 million.

To give you more color on these results, let me start with our ARR performance, which continues to be the bedrock of our SaaS model at CloudForge. Annual Recurring Revenue—or ARR—best captures the predictability and scalability of our platform. For Q3 FY2025, ending September 30th, our total ARR reached $452 million, up an impressive 29% year-over-year from $350 million in Q3 FY2024. This marks our 11th straight quarter of at least 25% YoY ARR growth, outpacing the public SaaS cohort's median of around 15-20%, as reported in recent Bessemer Venture Partners' State of the Cloud indices. Quarter-over-quarter, ARR grew 6.3% sequentially from $425 million at the end of Q2, which was slightly ahead of our internal guide of 5-6% due to stronger-than-expected expansions in our enterprise segment.

Breaking this down by cohort: New ACV adds contributed $28 million in new ARR, a 35% YoY increase, driven by 42 net new logos over $1 million ACV—our largest quarterly haul ever. Highlights include a landmark deal with a top-5 hyperscaler for our Kubernetes-native orchestration layer, rivaling the scale of Datadog's AWS integrations, and multi-year commitments from EMEA fintechs leveraging our SOC 2 Type II and FedRAMP Moderate authorizations.

Existing customer expansions added $22 million, fueled by a dollar-based net retention rate—or DBNR—of 118% for the quarter, consistent with our full-year target of 115-120%. This reflects classic SaaS land-and-expand dynamics: customers starting with our core PipelineForge product are rapidly adopting add-ons like AI CodeGuard for autonomous testing—our GenAI initiative that's seeing 40% attachment rates—and InfraForge for Terraform-as-a-Service. We've seen cohort retention for customers over $100k ARR hit 98% over the last 12 months, well above industry benchmarks from Pacific Crest's SaaS surveys.

Regionally, North America remains our growth engine at 65% of total ARR, delivering 32% YoY growth amid resilient enterprise IT budgets despite macro headwinds like elevated interest rates curbing smaller deals. EMEA surged 45% YoY to 22% of ARR, propelled by GDPR-aligned features and wins in DACH and UK financial services—think Commerzbank-scale deployments. APAC, now 13% of ARR, grew 25% YoY but decelerated QoQ to 4% due to FX volatility in JPY and softer China demand amid regulatory scrutiny on cloud providers; however, our Singapore hub and partnerships with Tencent Cloud are positioning us for reacceleration in H1 FY2026.

On trends, we've embedded strategic initiatives to sustain this momentum. Our Q2 launch of the AI Optimization Suite has driven 2.5x faster pipeline velocity for beta users, converting 70% to paid, echoing Snowflake's AI uptake playbook. We've also deepened integrations with GitHub Copilot and Azure DevOps, capturing share in the $50B+ DevOps market per Gartner forecasts. Churn remains pristine at 4% gross dollar retention—down from 5% a year ago—thanks to proactive CSM-led success plans and our 95% renewal rate on multi-year contracts.

Looking forward, we see Q4 YoY ARR growth in the 27-30% band, with sequential acceleration from Q4 seasonality and a $200 million pipeline of expansions. This positions us to lap easier comps in FY2026 while investing in R&D for edge computing and zero-trust security modules to fend off competitive pressures from GitLab Ultimate and Harness.

Next, turning to our liquidity position, which remains a cornerstone of our financial strength as we execute on our long-term growth strategy in the AI-driven SaaS workflow automation space. As of the end of Q3 FY2025, our cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments stood at $452 million, up 8% quarter-over-quarter from $420 million at the end of Q2. This marks our sixth consecutive quarter of sequential cash balance growth, reflecting the operating leverage inherent in our SaaS model as we scale.

In Q3, we generated $38 million in cash from operating activities, a 25% improvement year-over-year and our strongest quarterly cash generation to date. This was driven by our ARR reaching $452 million, up 29% YoY, with dollar-based net retention of 118%—fueled by upsells into our AI Workflow Engine, which now powers 65% of our top 100 customer accounts, similar to the expansion dynamics we've seen at peers like ServiceNow with their Now Assist LLM integrations.

Free cash flow, which we define as cash from operations less capital expenditures, came in at $32 million positive in the quarter—our first full quarter of sustained FCF positivity at scale. Capex remains disciplined at just 1.5% of revenue, primarily supporting data center expansions for our multi-tenant cloud infrastructure on AWS and Azure to handle the surge in GPU-intensive AI workloads.

On the cash burn front, our net cash burn rate has compressed dramatically to under $5 million per month in Q3, down from $18 million per month in Q3 FY2024. This 72% reduction is a testament to our Rule of 40 performance—we're tracking at 48 this quarter (29% growth + 19% non-GAAP operating margin)—as gross margins expanded to 82%, aided by API cost optimizations with partners like OpenAI and Anthropic.

At our current burn rate and conservative FCF projections, this translates to a cash runway exceeding 36 months as of Q3 end—well beyond the 24-month threshold we target for SaaS companies in our growth phase. Even stress-testing for a macroeconomic slowdown with 20% lower-than-expected net new ARR adds and flat NRR, our runway holds firm at 28 months. This visibility gives us tremendous optionality.

Regionally, our U.S. business, which represents 62% of ARR, continues to drive cash inflows with large enterprise wins like our $12 million deal with a Fortune 50 financial services firm, mirroring the hyperscaler momentum at Snowflake. EMEA grew ARR 45% YoY to $78 million, bolstered by GDPR-compliant AI features that accelerated land-and-expand in regulated verticals like healthcare and manufacturing—think expansions akin to UiPath's success in Europe. APAC, at 18% of ARR, faced 5% FX headwinds from a stronger USD but still delivered 22% constant-currency growth, with early traction in Japan via partnerships with local SIs.

Strategically, we're prioritizing cash deployment into high-ROI areas: 40% allocated to R&D for next-gen capabilities like agentic AI orchestration, where we're investing in proprietary fine-tuned models to reduce reliance on third-party LLMs and target 85% gross margins by FY2027; 30% to sales and marketing for mid-market expansion via our self-serve tier, aiming to double usage-based revenue from $45 million ARR; and reserving 20% for opportunistic tuck-in M&A, such as vertical-specific add-ons in legaltech or HRtech, much like Appian's bolt-on strategy.

Looking ahead to FY2026, we expect FCF to inflect to $150 million or 50% of non-GAAP operating income, extending our runway to indefinite as we approach cash flow neutrality on an annual basis. This positions CloudForge not just to weather any macro volatility—like the enterprise budget scrutiny we've seen industry-wide post-2022—but to capitalize on the $200 billion TAM for AI-augmented workflows, per Gartner estimates.

Moving on to customer acquisition cost, or CAC, trends, which continue to reflect the strength of our efficient growth engine here at CloudForge. CAC is calculated as our total sales and marketing expenses—including salaries, commissions, ad spend, content production, events, and partner programs—divided by the number of new customers acquired in the quarter. We report this on a blended basis across our self-serve SMB, mid-market, and enterprise segments, always tying it back to our LTV-to-CAC ratio and cohort payback periods.

In Q3 FY2025, our blended CAC came in at $1,180, a 21% year-over-year decline from $1,495 in Q3 FY2024, and a sequential improvement of 8% from $1,285 in Q2. This marks our sixth straight quarter of CAC compression, bringing our trailing 12-month average to $1,250—well below the SaaS industry benchmark of around $1,800 for high-growth players in the collaboration and workflow automation space, per our internal benchmarking against peers like Asana, Monday.com, and Smartsheet.

By segment: SMB/Self-Serve, which is 62% of new logos, CAC at $285, down 28% YoY from $395. This is driven by our product-led growth, or PLG, motion, where viral coefficients hit 1.35x—meaning each user brings 1.35 more via referrals and sharing. Freemium conversions accelerated to 14% from 9% YoY, fueled by our AI-powered workflow builder, which now has 40% adoption among free users.

Mid-Market, 24% of new logos: CAC of $4,200, improved 18% YoY. Content syndication and SEO traffic from our "Workflow AI Benchmarks" report series generated 25% more qualified leads at 30% lower cost per lead.

Enterprise, 14% of new logos: CAC at $28,500, down 15% YoY from $33,600. While higher due to dedicated AE-led motions, we're seeing payback shrink to 14 months from 18, thanks to multi-year deals averaging 2.8x net expansion in Year 1.

Regionally: North America, 72% of ARR, CAC at $1,050, our best-ever, with 24% YoY decline. Brand lift from our Super Bowl-adjacent digital campaign with AWS Marketplace integrations played a big role, capturing 15% more Fortune 1000 pipeline.

EMEA, 18% of ARR: $1,420 CAC, down 19% YoY, boosted by GDPR-compliant AI features and partnerships with local CSPs like OVHcloud, yielding a 2.5x ROI on channel spend.

APAC, 10% of ARR: $1,650 CAC, improved 12% YoY despite forex headwinds. Localized self-serve onboarding in Japanese and Mandarin drove 3x faster velocity, with Tencent Cloud co-marketing adding 200+ logos.

Powering these trends: PLG optimization with "ForgeAI Predict," our new in-app recommendation engine, which increased trial-to-paid conversion by 22%. This mirrors successes at companies like HubSpot, reducing top-of-funnel spend by 35% as organic channels now represent 48% of acquisitions.

Sales efficiency gains: Our Magic Number hit 1.2x, up from 0.9x YoY. We've layered in intent data from 6sense and G2, cutting unqualified leads by 40%, and shifted 30% of mid-market to inside sales.

Partner ecosystem expansion: AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Marketplace deals contributed 22% of new ARR at a CAC payback under 9 months—half our direct average. This is akin to Zoom's early marketplace playbook but supercharged with our API-first architecture.

Macro tailwinds helped too: Despite lingering economic caution, SaaS demand for AI automation remains resilient, with our win rates holding at 42% versus 38% industry average per Bessemer Venture Partners' State of the Cloud report.

Looking forward, we expect Q4 blended CAC to land around $1,100, with further compression from our Q4 launch of "Forge Enterprise Trials"—a low-touch path to enterprise that could shift 10% of logos from high-touch. Our LTV-to-CAC ratio sits comfortably at 4.8x, with median cohort payback at 13 months, giving us ample room to invest in growth while hitting Rule of 40 scores above 50%.

Shifting to free cash flow performance, which continues to be a hallmark of CloudForge's financial health and our ability to generate sustainable, high-quality cash flows in this competitive SaaS landscape. For Q3 FY2025, we delivered free cash flow of $32 million, representing about 21% of revenue and marking a significant improvement year-over-year. For the full fiscal year to date, free cash flow has been robust, putting us well ahead of our guided range and on track toward our long-term target of 30%+ FCF margins as we scale.

Key drivers start with revenue growth: Q3 total revenue of $152 million, up 37% year-over-year, driven primarily by ARR expansion and net revenue retention rate holding steady at 118% for the quarter—above our historical average—fueled by land-and-expand motions in our enterprise customer base. Large customers over $100K in ARR now represent 58% of total ARR, up from 52% a year ago, and contributed meaningfully to cash inflows through multi-year contracts and upsells on our AI-powered workflow automation suite, ForgeAI. Features like predictive resource allocation and no-code integrations drove a 35% attach rate among new logos and 18% expansion within existing accounts.

Operating cash flow hit $38 million in the quarter, thanks to disciplined working capital management. Days sales outstanding improved, reflecting faster collections from strengthened credit processes and the shift toward upfront payments in new enterprise deal structures—over 40% of Q3 ACVs included multi-year prepays. Unbilled deferred revenue, tied to our RPO, also converted efficiently.

Cost levers were impactful: We maintained GAAP gross margins at 82%, benefiting from economies of scale in our multi-tenant cloud architecture on AWS. By optimizing Kubernetes-based orchestration and shifting workloads to Graviton processors, we reduced hosting costs per seat even as we scaled AI workloads. Sales and marketing efficiency improved, with CAC payback dropping, allowing us to generate strong FCF per dollar of sales spend. This kept OpEx growth below revenue growth, helping our Rule of 40 score.

Regionally, North America contributed the bulk of FCF with strong growth, propelled by hyperscaler partnerships like our deepened integration with Microsoft Azure. APAC was a bright spot with ARR expansion, thanks to regulatory tailwinds in Japan and India. EMEA showed progress in verticals like financial services.

Strategically, we're deploying capital into share repurchases and R&D for next-gen features like agentic AI agents. Looking ahead, we expect continued FCF growth, assuming NRR above 110% and OpEx leverage.

Now, on our Lifetime Value to Customer Acquisition Cost—or LTV/CAC—ratio, which remains a north star for sustainable growth in our SaaS model. LTV represents the net present value of gross profit from a customer cohort over their expected lifetime, calculated as ARR per customer divided by churn rate, multiplied by our average gross margin of 82%. CAC is total sales and marketing spend divided by new customers added.

In Q3, our LTV/CAC ratio expanded to 4.3x, up from 3.9x in Q2 and 28% improved year-over-year from 3.4x. This puts us in the top quartile of public SaaS peers, benchmarking favorably against HubSpot and Snowflake. At current levels, this translates to an LTV of approximately $14,200 per customer—driven by average new logo ARR of $28K, cohort lifetime of 36 months, and CAC of $3,300, down 12% sequentially.

On CAC leverage: PLG motion now accounts for 42% of new ACV, slashing onboarding costs. AI-powered lead scoring boosted conversions. We've rationalized paid channels and improved sales efficiency, with payback periods compressing to 14 months.

LTV expansion from sticky dynamics: NRR at 118%, with upsells into AI Forecasting adding value. Churn down to 0.9% monthly for enterprise. Gross margins up to 82% with consumption-based pricing.

Regionally, North America at 4.6x, EMEA climbing to 4.1x, APAC at 3.4x but improving with partnerships.

This ratio underscores our Rule of 50 discipline. We're targeting 4.8x to 5.0x by year-end through PLG scaling, GenAI sales outreach, and enterprise expansion.

Next, our full-year fiscal 2025 revenue guidance, which we're updating today to reflect Q3 execution and momentum. Entering Q3, we guided to $580 million to $590 million, about 38% YoY growth. Q3 exceeded at $152 million, up 37% YoY and 8% QoQ—strongest sequential in two years. Driven by 42% new ACV increase from enterprises, NRR at 128%, RPO up 52% to $1.2 billion.

We're raising to $605 million to $615 million, implying 41% to 43% YoY at midpoint $610 million, with Q4 $158-165 million.

Drivers: NRR averaging 127%, new logo ACV up 45%, multi-product adoption at 65%. AI Orchestrator contributing 15% of bookings, integrations with Snowflake and Databricks. Average ACV up 12%.

Regional: Americas 41% growth, EMEA 35%, APAC 28%.

Macro resilience in DevOps market. Prioritizing sales capacity and R&D.

Assumes no major M&A, current FX.

Turning to the Rule of 40, which sums YoY ARR growth plus non-GAAP EBITDA margin. For FY2025 to date, CloudForge delivered 48%, balancing growth and profitability.

ARR growth at 29% YoY to $452 million, from new logos, expansions (NDR 118%), large deals. EBITDA margin at 19%, expanded via gross margins at 82%, S&M at 38% of revenue, G&A 12%. FCF margin strong.

Outperforms peers, positions us well. Regional: NA 32%, EMEA 25%, APAC 45%. R&D yields like agentic AI boosting ACV.

GTM evolution, customer stickiness. Guide FY2026 45-48%, ARR 27-30%, margins 17-19%.

Finally, on operating margin: non-GAAP at 28.4% for Q3, 310 bps YoY improvement from 25.3%, 120 bps sequential. Seventh straight quarter of expansion.

Drivers: Revenue up 37% to $152M, ARR 29% to $452M, NRR 118%. Gross margin 82.1% from cloud optimizations—ARM instances reduced costs 22%, GenAI support cut PS 15%.

S&M 36% of revenue, down from 41%: PLG at 14.2% conversion, CAC down 18%. Enterprise payback 14 months. Regional leverage, EMEA strong.

R&D 22% but 1.8x ROI: Edge module, headcount optimization. G&A 7%, offset forex.

Forward to mid-30s by FY2027 via pricing, AI savings.

That covers our financial highlights. Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Elena Vasquez for a technology update.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Mike. This quarter, we made significant progress in advancing our AI capabilities and further integrating them into our core platform. We are seeing strong adoption of our new AI-powered features, which are driving increased user engagement and improved customer outcomes. We've also focused on enhancing our platform's security and scalability to meet the growing demands of our enterprise customers.

And now Lisa Wong will provide an update on the product roadmap.

Lisa Wong:
Thank you, Elena. We have been focusing on the user experience of our products and are excited to announce the launch of ForgeAI Predict. This new feature significantly improves trial-to-paid conversions and pipeline velocity. We are seeing strong adoption of this feature, which aligns with our product strategy.

Tom Harris:
Thank you, Lisa. This quarter our focus was on increasing our brand awareness and lead generation through targeted digital campaigns and strategic partnerships. We saw a 25% increase in website traffic and a 30% increase in qualified leads, demonstrating the effectiveness of our marketing initiatives.

Rachel Kim:
Thank you, Tom. We are committed to delivering exceptional customer experiences and this quarter, we focused on improving our customer support and onboarding processes. As a result, we have seen a 15% increase in customer satisfaction scores.

Mike Patel:
Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to register a question, please press star one one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from Raimo Lenschow with Barclays.

Raimo Lenschow:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of ForgeAI on your overall growth, what kind of attach rates are you seeing, how it compares to your initial expectations, what's the competitive landscape like, and how do you plan to differentiate yourselves?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks for the question, Raimo. ForgeAI has been transformative for our growth, contributing over 15% of new bookings this quarter and accelerating ARR expansions by driving 2.5x faster pipeline velocity. Attach rates are at 40% across new logos, well above our initial expectations of 25-30%, with 70% of beta users converting to paid. Compared to peers, we're seeing uptake similar to Snowflake's Cortex but tailored for DevOps.

The competitive landscape includes GitLab and Harness, but they lack our depth in agentic AI orchestration. We differentiate through proprietary fine-tuned models, multi-cloud agnosticism with AWS/Azure/GCP integrations, and zero-trust security—positioning us to capture more of the $50B DevOps TAM.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Kirk Materne with Evercore ISI.

Kirk Materne:
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region, what are your key target markets, what are your expected ROI from these investments, and what are the key challenges you anticipate?

Sarah Chen:
Great question, Kirk. International expansion is a priority, with APAC as a key focus representing 13% of ARR but growing 25% YoY. Target markets are Japan, India, and Singapore, leveraging partnerships like Tencent Cloud and NTT for localized self-serve. We expect 2.5-3x ROI on investments within 18 months, driven by constant-currency growth and NRR above 115%.

Challenges include FX volatility and regulatory scrutiny in China, but our Singapore hub and data sovereignty features mitigate these. We're ramping with Mandarin interfaces and SI partnerships to reaccelerate in H1 FY2026.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Brad Zelnick with Wolfe Research.

Brad Zelnick:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, what's the trend you are seeing in NRR, what are your strategies to improve customer retention, what's the impact of pricing changes on churn, and what are your long-term targets for NRR?

Mike Patel:
Thanks, Brad. Churn remains low at 4% gross dollar retention, down from 5% YoY, thanks to proactive CSM-led success plans and 95% renewal on multi-year contracts. NRR is stable at 118%, consistent with our target.

Retention strategies include AI-powered health scoring and upsell playbooks emphasizing ForgeAI modules. Pricing changes—modest 8-10% uplifts—have had no negative impact, actually boosting expansions. Long-term, we target 120-122% NRR as agentic AI drives more value.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Saket Kalia with Barclays.

Saket Kalia:
Can you provide more color on customer acquisition costs (CAC) and payback periods for new customers?

Mike Patel:
Sure, Saket. Blended CAC is $1,180, down 21% YoY, with SMB at $285, mid-market $4,200, and enterprise $28,500—all compressing. Median cohort payback is 13-14 months, down from 18, thanks to PLG (48% organic acquisitions), partner marketplaces (9-month payback), and 118% NRR funding expansions. This efficiency supports our 4.3x LTV/CAC.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Sarah Chen for closing remarks.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
aspects: ARR growth (YoY and QoQ): Report actual ARR and percentage growth.
Cash runway: Discuss cash position and expected cash runway.

LTV/CAC ratio: Report the Lifetime Value to Customer Acquisition Cost ratio.
Full-year revenue guidance: Provide revenue guidance for the full fiscal year.
Rule of 40: Report the Rule of 40 metric (Revenue Growth + Profit Margin).
Operating margin: Report operating margin and explain drivers.
